context:
Compose with existing SchemaV2Validator (schema.py) as the first structural check.
If SchemaV2Validator raises, record FAIL and short-circuit structural checks.
Otherwise run all three tiers in sequence.

Benchmark specs are hardcoded from reference runs (not dynamically derived from
benchmark modules) - dynamic derivation creates transitive import issues and makes
the validator less self-contained.

Two-tier severity model:
  FAIL = mathematical impossibility or known-bad value (corrupted result)
  WARN = suspicious-but-plausible (degraded result, may still be valid)

The CLI script uses validate_file / validate_directory from the core module
directly - no duplication of logic.
description:
The live integration test suite produces JSON result files after each benchmark
run but there is no systematic way to evaluate whether those files are
structurally sound, complete, and believable. A silent failure - missing queries,
zero-time measurements, wrong row counts - can pass undetected.

This task implements a three-tier validator (structural → completeness →
believability) using the 20 DuckDB SF1 reference runs as ground-truth baselines.
The validator serves three consumers:
  1. CI/post-run scripts: batch-validate a results directory, non-zero exit on failure
  2. Live integration tests: importable function called after running a benchmark
  3. Interactive analysis: MCP tool for Claude-assisted review

Three-tier check system:
  STRUCTURAL  - schema version, required keys, cross-field math, non-negative
                timings, percentile ordering, valid phase enums
  COMPLETENESS - expected query IDs for known benchmarks, measurement iterations
                 present, power phase completed, tables object when required
  BELIEVABILITY - avg between min/max, geomean plausible, success rate above
                  benchmark floor, SF1 row counts within 1%, no duplicate
                  (id, iter, stream) combos

Reference DuckDB SF1 files live in benchmark_runs/results/ and match
the glob *_sf1_duckdb_*_2026*.json (55 files total). There are 20 current
benchmark IDs plus 8 legacy aliases (e.g., star_schema→ssb,
amplab_big_data→amplab, h2o_database→h2odb, tpc_di→tpcdi,
joinorderbenchmark→joinorder, nyc_taxi_olap→nyctaxi,
flight_data_olap→flightdata, data_vault→datavault).
The validator must handle both current and legacy benchmark IDs.

anti_patterns.dont: import benchmark modules (tpch, tpcds, etc.) from benchmark_specs.py
anti_patterns.why: hardcode the expected query ID sets to keep the validator self-contained and fast
return IntegrityReport with FAIL status so callers can decide how to handle
call schema_validator.validate(raw) as the first structural check

register_analytics_tools() signature in analytics.py - only ADD a new @mcp.tool() inside it
